title: Integrating targeting behaviour and spatial effects to standardize CPUE in a multispecies deep-water fishery
content:
Abstract
Catch per unit effort (CPUE) is widely used to derive abundance indices, yet inference is often biased in multispecies fisheries where targeting behaviour and nonrandom spatial effort allocation affect catchability. Here, we applied a CPUE standardization framework that integrates targeting behaviour and spatial dependence to estimate annual abundance indices for commercially important stocks exploited by a deep-water multispecies fishery in the Azores over the last two decades. Targeting was represented using two composition-based approaches, namely categorical fishing tactics derived from catch composition and a Direct Principal Component method based on principal components of catch composition. For each species, Generalized Additive Mixed Models with a Tweedie distribution were fitted to trip-level catches with an effort offset, including smooth spatial effects and depth alongside operational covariates. Spatial location and depth consistently explained a substantial fraction of variability in catch rates, and incorporating targeting covariates generally reduced AIC and residual deviance, and improved residual-diagnostic behaviour across species, particularly for stocks with high zero-catch frequency. Interannual trajectories were broadly consistent among formulations, although differences were evident in peak magnitude, relative level, and uncertainty for some species. Spatial predictions revealed pronounced, species-specific hotspots, emphasising the importance of explicitly modelling spatial structure when deriving indices from fishery-dependent data. The approach provides a basis for constructing CPUE-based abundance indices in multispecies fisheries where adaptive targeting and spatially clustered exploitation are common.
